text:
maya: customer opened a ticket: intermittent 503s from EU clients to /v1/generate. they supplied a single request_id that came back in the response body: 0a1b2c3d9ef4a7c. timeline they gave: 2025-12-02T18:22:45Z. asking if infra can locate server logs.

sasha: thanks — can you confirm whether the client set an X-Request-Id header? also ask them for the raw response headers and the exact curl they used (with Authorization redacted). without client-set request id it's harder to correlate across proxies and CDN.

maya: customer says they didn't set X-Request-Id, only saw req id in response JSON. payload was ~2.3k tokens, EU region, no streaming. i asked for a repro curl and debug bundle.

ryan: did a quick search in Kibana against prod hot indices:
```
request_id:"0a1b2c3d9ef4a7c"
```
no matches. note: our hot index retention is 30 days by default. that timestamp is ~380 days ago -> likely expired from hot cluster.

sasha: if hot logs expired, two options:
1) customer has log-archive (S3) enabled for their org -> we can run an archive retrieval
2) customer reproduces now and provides a debug bundle + client X-Request-Id so we can capture the new event

infra-bot: NOTICE: hot indices retention policy = 30d. Archived log retention for orgs with log-archive add-on = 1 year in S3. Archive retrieval requires org owner consent and takes 24-72 hours.

maya: confirmed the org is on paid hosted tier but NOT subscribed to log-archive addon.

ryan: since we can't pull the original row, ask them to repro with these exact asks:
- run a curl including a client-generated X-Request-Id header, e.g. X-Request-Id: cust-20251202-r1
- include full response headers and body
- timestamp in ISO8601 UTC of the request
- indicate whether they were using streaming, chunked transfer, or standard request
- temporarily disable client retries so we get first-failure behavior

Example curl we gave them to run (they should paste full terminal output):
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Request-Id: cust-20251202-r1"
  -d '{"input":"<their prompt>", "max_tokens":512}'
```

sasha: request they also attach a debug bundle (instructions): include raw client logs showing timestamps, the full HTTP response (headers + body), and the terminal output of the curl run. if they can reproduce repeatedly, ask them to produce a sequence of X-Request-Id values so we can look for patterns.

ryan: when we have a repro request_id we will run these queries in Kibana (hot) or ask infra to scan S3 (archive):
KQL for HTTP failures:
```
(request_id:"cust-20251202-r1" OR request_id:"0a1b2c3d9ef4a7c") AND http.status_code:503
```
Lucene (wider):
```
request_id:(cust-20251202-r1 OR 0a1b2c3d9ef4a7c) AND status:503 AND region:eu*
```
Trace window (by timestamp range):
```
trace_id:* AND @timestamp:["2025-12-02T18:20:00" TO "2025-12-02T18:30:00"]
```
If we need an archive pull we'll include the org owner in the consent flow and open a retrieval ticket. remind customer that archive pulls are slower (24-72h) and billable for some orgs.

maya: customer replied they can reproduce and will run the curl + bundle this afternoon and include the X-Request-Id. i'll paste results here when it comes in.

sasha: once they post the new request_id and attach the bundle, include it in the internal support ticket and ping me. if archive retrieval becomes necessary i'll file the S3 pull and flag it as high-priority — note: we need explicit org owner approval.

ryan: small troubleshooting tips to give the customer:
- toggle backoff/retries off while reproducing
- include the Authorization header (redacted) in the debug bundle so we can see auth method used
- if possible, reproduce from a different client location (e.g. another EU zone) to rule out regional infra issues

maya: cool — i'll wait for their bundle. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
